25 A source emits a progressive sound wave in the horizontal direction. The wave travels away from
the source in a direction towards the right.
The graph shows the variation of the displacement of the particles from their equilibrium positions
with distance from the source at a particular instant in time. Displacements to the right of the
equilibrium positions are shown as positive.
displacement
0
0
distance
Y
Position Y represents the displacement of a particle in the sound wave at a particular distance
from the source at this instant.
Which statement about the motion of this particle is correct?
A
The particle is moving away from the source.
B
The particle is moving towards the source.
C
The particle is moving upwards.
D
The particle is moving downwards.

hints: Notice Y is on the rising slope of the displacement-distance graph where displacement is negative but slope $dy/dx$ is positive.
Remember sound is a longitudinal wave travelling to the right, so particles vibrate horizontally left-right, not upwards or downwards.
Imagine the whole wave pattern shifting a little to the right: a fixed point Y will next take the value from just to its left, which is more negative, so it must move left.
walkthrough: Identify the wave type: sound is a longitudinal progressive wave travelling towards the right, away from the source on the left.
Read the graph correctly: it is a snapshot of particle displacement $y$ against distance $x$. Positive $y$ means displaced to the right, negative $y$ means displaced to the left.
Locate Y: it has negative displacement and lies on a section where $y$ increases with $x$, so the gradient $dy/dx$ is positive.
Use the rule for a wave moving in the $+x$ direction: particle velocity is opposite in sign to the spatial gradient, $v_{particle} \propto -dy/dx$.
Apply it at Y: $dy/dx > 0$ so $v_{particle} < 0$. Negative velocity means motion to the left, back towards the source.

A.explanation: The particle is not moving to the right. The positive slope at Y combined with rightward wave motion gives a negative velocity, which is to the left.

B.explanation: The slope at Y is positive and the wave moves right, so the particle velocity is to the left, which is back towards the source on the left.

C.explanation: The particle does not move up. Sound is longitudinal so vibration is horizontal, and the vertical axis shows right-left displacement, not up-down position.

D.explanation: The particle does not move down. The up-down appearance is only the plotted displacement-distance graph of a horizontal longitudinal vibration.
